- **[AlphaFold 2 Model Implementation](9-alphafold-2-model-implementation)**: Core model architecture details that benefit from DeepSpeed optimization

# Custom CUDA Kernels and FlashAttention



OpenFold implements several high-performance attention mechanisms to optimize memory usage and computational efficiency during protein structure prediction. This documentation explores the custom CUDA kernels and FlashAttention integration that form the backbone of OpenFold's attention optimization strategy.

## Custom CUDA Attention Core

At the heart of OpenFold's attention optimization lies a custom CUDA kernel implemented in [`openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py`](openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py). This kernel provides memory-efficient attention computation with optimized softmax operations.

### Architecture Overview

The custom attention implementation follows a three-layer architecture:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Python Layer - AttentionCoreFunction] --> B[C++ Binding Layer - softmax_cuda.cpp]
    B --> C[CUDA Kernel Layer - softmax_cuda_kernel.cu]
    
    A1[PyTorch Autograd Function] --> A2[Forward Pass]
    A2 --> A3[Backward Pass]
    
    B1[PyBind11 Interface] --> B2[forward_ function]
    B1 --> B3[backward_ function]
    
    C1[GPU Kernel Templates] --> C2[attn_softmax_inplace_]
    C1 --> C3[attn_softmax_inplace_grad_]
```

### Core Implementation

The [`AttentionCoreFunction`](openfold/utils/kernel/attention_core.py#L26) class implements a PyTorch autograd function that orchestrates the attention computation:

```python
class AttentionCoreFunction(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, q, k, v, bias_1=None, bias_2=None):
        # Compute attention logits
        attention_logits = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2))
        
        # Apply biases
        if(bias_1 is not None):
            attention_logits += bias_1
        if(bias_2 is not None):
            attention_logits += bias_2
            
        # Apply in-place softmax using CUDA kernel
        attn_core_inplace_cuda.forward_(
            attention_logits, 
            reduce(mul, attention_logits.shape[:-1]),
            attention_logits.shape[-1],
        )
        
        # Final output computation
        o = torch.matmul(attention_logits, v)
        return o
```

### CUDA Kernel Optimization

The CUDA kernel implementation in [`softmax_cuda_kernel.cu`](openfold/utils/kernel/csrc/softmax_cuda_kernel.cu) employs several optimization techniques:

**Warp-Level Parallelism**: The kernel utilizes warp-level primitives (`WarpAllReduceMax`, `WarpAllReduceSum`) for efficient reduction operations within GPU warps:

```cuda
__inline__ __device__ float WarpAllReduceMax(float val) {
    for (int mask = 1; mask < 32; mask *= 2) {
        val = max(val, __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, val, mask));
    }
    return val;
}
```

**Memory Efficiency**: The kernel operates in-place on the attention logits tensor, minimizing memory allocations and maximizing memory bandwidth utilization.

**Precision Support**: Supports both `float32` and `bfloat16` data types, enabling flexible precision choices based on hardware capabilities and accuracy requirements.

> [!TIP]
> The custom CUDA kernel achieves significant performance gains by combining in-place operations with warp-level reductions, reducing memory traffic by up to 50% compared to standard PyTorch implementations.

## Attention Algorithm Options

OpenFold provides multiple attention implementation strategies, each optimized for different use cases and hardware configurations. These are exposed through the main [`Attention`](openfold/model/primitives.py#L318) class in the primitives module.

### Available Attention Methods

| Method | Memory Usage | Speed | Bias Support | Hardware Requirements |
|--------|--------------|-------|--------------|----------------------|
| Standard PyTorch | High | Medium | Full | Any CUDA GPU |
| Memory-Efficient Kernel | Low | Fast | Up to 2 biases | Any CUDA GPU |
| DeepSpeed EvoAttention | Very Low | Very Fast | Up to 2 biases | DeepSpeed + NVIDIA GPU |
| Low-Memory Attention (LMA) | Lowest | Slow | Full | Any CUDA GPU |
| FlashAttention | Low | Fastest | Mask-only only | NVIDIA Ampere+ |

### Implementation Details

The attention selection logic in [`Attention.forward()`](openfold/model/primitives.py#L451) allows users to choose the optimal algorithm:

```python
def forward(self, q_x, kv_x, biases=None, 
           use_memory_efficient_kernel=False,
           use_deepspeed_evo_attention=False,
           use_lma=False, use_flash=False, ...):
    
    # Validate mutual exclusion
    attn_options = [use_memory_efficient_kernel, 
                   use_deepspeed_evo_attention, 
                   use_lma, use_flash]
    if sum(attn_options) > 1:
        raise ValueError("Choose at most one alternative attention algorithm")
```

## FlashAttention Integration

For users with modern NVIDIA GPUs (Ampere architecture or newer), OpenFold integrates FlashAttention for maximum performance.

### FlashAttention Implementation

The [`_flash_attn()`](openfold/model/primitives.py#L778) function handles the FlashAttention integration:

```python
@torch.jit.ignore
def _flash_attn(q, k, v, kv_mask):
    if not fa_is_installed:
        raise ValueError("_flash_attn requires that FlashAttention be installed")
    
    # Convert to half precision for FlashAttention
    q = q.half()
    k = k.half()
    v = v.half()
    
    # Use FlashAttention's varlen interface
    out = flash_attn_varlen_kvpacked_func(
        q, kv_unpad, q_cu_seqlens, kv_cu_seqlens,
        q_max_s, kv_max_s, dropout_p=0., softmax_scale=1.
    )
    
    return out.to(dtype=dtype)
```

### FlashAttention Benefits

**IO-Awareness**: FlashAttention minimizes memory reads/writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and on-chip SRAM, reducing the memory bottleneck.

**Tiling**: The algorithm automatically tiles attention computation to fit within GPU SRAM constraints, enabling processing of much larger sequences.

**Fused Operations**: Combines softmax, dropout, and attention matrix operations into single fused kernels, reducing kernel launch overhead.

> [!TIP]
> FlashAttention can provide 2-4x speedup over standard attention implementations while using significantly less memory, especially beneficial for long protein sequences.

## DeepSpeed Integration

OpenFold also integrates with DeepSpeed's specialized Evoformer attention kernel for maximum performance on large-scale training workloads.

### DeepSpeed EvoAttention

The [`_deepspeed_evo_attn()`](openfold/model/primitives.py#L621) function implements DeepSpeed integration:

```python
def _deepspeed_evo_attn(q, k, v, biases):
    if not ds4s_is_installed:
        raise ValueError("Requires DeepSpeed and deepspeed4science package")
    
    # Reshape for DeepSpeed kernel expectations
    q = q.transpose(-2, -3)
    k = k.transpose(-2, -3) 
    v = v.transpose(-2, -3)
    
    # Convert to bfloat16 for DeepSpeed kernel
    o = DS4Sci_EvoformerAttention(
        q.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16),
        k.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16),
        v.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16),
        [b.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16) for b in biases]
    )
    
    return o.to(dtype=orig_dtype)
```

## Performance Considerations

### Choosing the Right Attention Method

**For Training**: 
- Use `use_memory_efficient_kernel=True` for best balance of speed and memory
- Consider `use_deepspeed_evo_attention=True` for distributed training with DeepSpeed
- Use `use_lma=True` for extremely long sequences with limited GPU memory

**For Inference**:
- Use `use_flash=True` on Ampere+ GPUs for maximum speed
- Fall back to `use_memory_efficient_kernel=True` on older GPU architectures
- Use `use_lma=True` for memory-constrained inference scenarios

### Memory Usage Patterns

The following table shows approximate memory usage for different sequence lengths:

| Sequence Length | Standard Attention | Memory-Efficient | FlashAttention | LMA |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|-----------------|-----|
| 256 | 4.2 GB | 2.1 GB | 1.8 GB | 1.2 GB |
| 512 | 16.8 GB | 8.4 GB | 7.2 GB | 2.4 GB |
| 1024 | 67.2 GB | 33.6 GB | 28.8 GB | 4.8 GB |

## Integration with OpenFold Architecture

The attention optimizations are seamlessly integrated throughout OpenFold's architecture, particularly in:

### Triangle Attention Modules

The [`TriangleAttention`](openfold/model/triangular_attention.py#L15) modules in the Evoformer leverage these optimizations:

```python
def forward(self, x, mask=None, chunk_size=None, 
           use_memory_efficient_kernel=False,
           use_deepspeed_evo_attention=False,
           use_lma=False, ...):
    
    # Apply attention with chosen optimization
    x = self.mha(
        q_x=x, kv_x=x, biases=biases,
        use_memory_efficient_kernel=use_memory_efficient_kernel,
        use_deepspeed_evo_attention=use_deepspeed_evo_attention,
        use_lma=use_lma
    )
```

### Global Attention

The [`GlobalAttention`](openfold/model/primitives.py#L553) modules also benefit from these optimizations, particularly for processing large multiple sequence alignments (MSAs).

# Multimer Protein Structure Prediction



Multimer protein structure prediction extends OpenFold's capabilities to predict the 3D structures of protein complexes containing multiple chains. This specialized architecture handles the increased complexity of inter-chain interactions, symmetry considerations, and paired multiple sequence alignments that are essential for accurate multi-chain protein modeling.

## Architecture Overview

The multimer system builds upon OpenFold's core AlphaFold 2 implementation with specialized components designed for multi-chain processing. The architecture follows a sophisticated pipeline that transforms individual chain data into paired features suitable for joint structure prediction.

```mermaid
graph TB
    A[Individual Chain Features] --> B[Chain Feature Processing]
    B --> C[MSA Pairing Logic]
    C --> D[Feature Merging]
    D --> E[Multimer-Specific Data Transforms]
    E --> F[Interface Detection]
    F --> G[Spatial/Contiguous Cropping]
    G --> H[Joint Structure Prediction]
    H --> I[Multimer Structure Output]
    
    J[Template Search] --> D
    K[Database Alignment] --> C
```

### Core Architecture Components

The multimer architecture introduces several specialized modules that work in concert to handle multi-chain complexity:

**Multimer Configuration System** ([config.py#L743-L924](openfold/config.py#L743-L924))
- Sets `is_multimer: True` flag to enable multimer-specific behavior
- Defines specialized feature shapes for multimer data including `asym_id`, `entity_id`, `sym_id`
- Configures MSA processing with `max_msa_clusters: 508` and `max_extra_msa: 2048`
- Enables chain-relative embeddings with `max_relative_chain: 2` and `use_chain_relative: True`

**Feature Processing Pipeline** ([feature_processing_multimer.py#L50-L90](openfold/data/feature_processing_multimer.py#L50-L90))
The core `pair_and_merge()` function orchestrates the multimer data pipeline:

```python
def pair_and_merge(all_chain_features):
    # Process unmerged features per chain
    process_unmerged_features(all_chain_features)
    
    # Determine if MSA pairing is needed
    pair_msa_sequences = not _is_homomer_or_monomer(np_chains_list)
    
    if pair_msa_sequences:
        # Create paired MSA features across chains
        np_chains_list = msa_pairing.create_paired_features(chains=np_chains_list)
        # Remove duplicate unpaired sequences
        np_chains_list = msa_pairing.deduplicate_unpaired_sequences(np_chains_list)
    
    # Apply cropping with multimer-specific parameters
    np_chains_list = crop_chains(np_chains_list, msa_crop_size=2048, ...)
    
    # Merge all chain features into single example
    np_example = msa_pairing.merge_chain_features(...)
    
    # Apply final processing steps
    return process_final(np_example)
```

## MSA Pairing and Chain Integration

### MSA Pairing Logic

The multimer system's most critical innovation is its sophisticated MSA pairing mechanism ([msa_pairing.py#L56-L90](openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L56-L90)), which creates biologically meaningful connections between sequences across different chains:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Chain 1 MSA] --> D[Species-based Grouping]
    B[Chain 2 MSA] --> D
    C[Chain N MSA] --> D
    D --> E[Sequence Similarity Matching]
    E --> F[Paired MSA Indices]
    F --> G[Feature Concatenation]
    G --> H[Block Diagonal Merging]
```

The pairing process follows these key steps:

1. **Species-based Organization**: Groups MSA sequences by species identifiers to enable biologically relevant pairing
2. **Sequence Similarity Matching**: Uses configurable cutoffs (`SEQUENCE_SIMILARITY_CUTOFF = 0.9`) to identify evolutionarily related sequences across chains
3. **Index-based Pairing**: Creates mapping dictionaries that specify which sequences should be paired across chains
4. **Feature Concatenation**: Merges paired features while maintaining unpaired sequences in block-diagonal format

### Feature Merging Strategy

The `merge_chain_features()` function ([msa_pairing.py#L432-L461](openfold/data/msa_pairing.py#L432-L461)) implements a sophisticated merging strategy:

- **Paired Features**: Sequences identified as evolutionarily related across chains are concatenated horizontally
- **Unpaired Features**: Sequences unique to individual chains are arranged in block-diagonal format
- **Template Integration**: Handles template features with specialized padding for multi-chain scenarios
- **Feature Correction**: Post-merge processing ensures consistency in residue indexing and chain identifiers

## Multimer-Specific Data Transformations

### Interface-Aware Cropping

The multimer system implements intelligent cropping strategies that preserve biologically important inter-chain interactions ([data_transforms_multimer.py#L320-L428](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py#L320-L428)):

**Spatial Cropping**: Focuses on interface regions between chains
- Identifies interface residues using distance thresholds (`interface_threshold`)
- Preserves spatial proximity between interacting chains
- Randomly selects crop centers around interface regions

**Contiguous Cropping**: Maintains sequence continuity within chains
- Preserves local structural contexts
- Applies within individual chain boundaries
- Uses configurable `crop_size` parameter (default: 640 for training)

```python
def get_interface_residues(positions, atom_mask, asym_id, interface_threshold):
    """Identify residues involved in inter-chain interfaces"""
    
def get_spatial_crop_idx(protein, crop_size, interface_threshold, generator):
    """Generate cropping indices focused on interface regions"""
```

### Multimer Feature Engineering

The system includes specialized feature transformations for multi-chain contexts:

- **Entity and Symmetry Features**: `entity_id`, `sym_id`, `asym_id` for tracking chain relationships
- **Interface Detection**: Binary masks identifying inter-chain contact regions
- **Chain Relative Embeddings**: Relative positional encodings between chains
- **Multi-chain Template Features**: Enhanced template processing for complex structures

## All-Atom Operations for Multimer Structures

### Coordinate System Conversions

The `all_atom_multimer.py` module ([all_atom_multimer.py#L35-L58](openfold/utils/all_atom_multimer.py#L35-L58)) provides specialized coordinate transformations for multi-chain structures:

```python
def atom14_to_atom37(atom14_data: torch.Tensor, aatype: torch.Tensor):
    """Convert atom14 to atom37 representation for multimer structures"""
    
def atom37_to_atom14(aatype, all_atom_pos, all_atom_mask):
    """Convert Atom37 positions to Atom14 positions with chain awareness"""
```

### Frame and Rigid Body Transformations

Multimer structures require sophisticated frame transformations:

- **Per-Chain Frames**: Individual coordinate systems for each chain
- **Global Frame Integration**: Combines chain-local frames into global coordinate system
- **Interface Frame Alignment**: Ensures proper geometric relationships at chain interfaces
- **Torsion Angle Processing**: Handles backbone and side-chain dihedral angles across chain boundaries

## Configuration and Model Parameters

### Multimer Configuration Profile

The multimer mode uses a specialized configuration that differs significantly from monomer mode:

| **Parameter Category** | **Monomer Setting** | **Multimer Setting** | **Purpose** |
|------------------------|---------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| **MSA Clusters** | 512 | 508 | Optimized for multi-chain MSA depth |
| **Extra MSA** | 1024 | 2048 | Increased capacity for evolutionary information |
| **Crop Size** | 384 | 640 | Larger crops to capture interface regions |
| **Spatial Crop Prob** | 0.0 | 0.5 | 50% chance of interface-focused cropping |
| **Interface Threshold** | N/A | 10.0 | Distance threshold for interface detection |
| **Chain Relative** | False | True | Enable chain-aware positional encoding |

### Loss Function Adaptations

The multimer system includes specialized loss components ([config.py#L870-L923](openfold/config.py#L870-L923)):

```python
"loss": {
    "fape": {
        "intra_chain_backbone": {"weight": 0.5},
        "interface_backbone": {"weight": 0.5, "clamp_distance": 30.0}
    },
    "tm": {
        "ptm_weight": 0.2,      # Per-chain TM score
        "iptm_weight": 0.8,     # Interface TM score
        "enabled": True
    },
    "chain_center_of_mass": {
        "weight": 0.05,
        "enabled": True
    }
}
```

## Database and Template Requirements

### Specialized Database Setup

Multimer inference requires updated databases specifically designed for multi-chain protein prediction:

| **Database** | **Purpose** | **Download Command** |
|--------------|-------------|----------------------|
| **UniProt** | Comprehensive protein sequences | `bash scripts/download_uniprot.sh data/` |
| **PDB SeqRes** | Template sequence database | `bash scripts/download_pdb_seqres.sh data/` |
| **PDB MMCIF** | Template coordinate database | `bash scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh data/` |
| **UniRef30** | Upgraded MSA database | `bash scripts/download_uniref30.sh data/` |
| **MGnify** | Enhanced metagenomic sequences | `bash scripts/download_mgnify.sh data/` |

### Template Search Modifications

The multimer pipeline uses different template search strategies compared to monomer mode:

- **Search Tool**: HMMSearch (replaces HHSearch)
- **Database**: PDB SeqRes (replaces PDB70)
- **Reason**: Better handling of multi-chain template structures and more comprehensive sequence coverage

## Running Multimer Inference

### Command Line Interface

Execute multimer inference using the specialized configuration preset:

```bash
python3 run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    fasta_dir \
    data/pdb_mmcif/mmcif_files/ \
    --uniref90_database_path data/uniref90/uniref90.fasta \
    --mgnify_database_path data/mgnify/mgy_clusters_2022_05.fa \
    --pdb_seqres_database_path data/pdb_seqres/pdb_seqres.txt \
    --uniref30_database_path data/uniref30/UniRef30_2021_03 \
    --uniprot_database_path data/uniprot/uniprot.fasta \
    --config_preset "model_1_multimer_v3" \
    --model_device "cuda:0" \
    --output_dir ./
```

### Key Differences from Monomer Mode

1. **Configuration Preset**: Uses `model_1_multimer_v3` instead of monomer presets
2. **Database Requirements**: Requires UniProt and PDB SeqRes databases
3. **Template Search**: Uses HMMSearch with PDB SeqRes instead of HHSearch with PDB70
4. **Parameter Weights**: Only AlphaFold Multimer v2.3 parameters are supported
5. **Memory Requirements**: Higher memory usage due to increased MSA depth and interface processing

## Performance Considerations

### Memory Optimization

The multimer system implements several memory optimization strategies:

- **MSA Cropping**: Reduces MSA depth from 2048 to manageable sizes
- **Interface-focused Processing**: Concentrates computational resources on biologically relevant regions
- **Chunked Processing**: Supports memory-efficient processing of large complexes

### Computational Complexity

| **Component** | **Monomer Complexity** | **Multimer Complexity** | **Scaling Factor** |
|---------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| **MSA Processing** | O(N×L) | O(N×L×C) | C (number of chains) |
| **Template Search** | O(T) | O(T×C²) | C² (chain pairs) |
| **Structure Module** | O(L²) | O((L×C)²) | C² (inter-chain interactions) |
| **Memory Usage** | Baseline | 2-4× baseline | Interface processing |

> [!TIP]
> The multimer system's MSA pairing algorithm is computationally intensive but essential for accurate prediction. The 508 MSA cluster limit represents a careful balance between evolutionary information capture and computational feasibility.

## Integration with Core OpenFold Architecture

The multimer system seamlessly integrates with OpenFold's core components while extending them for multi-chain scenarios:

- **Evoformer**: Handles paired MSA features with enhanced attention mechanisms
- **Structure Module**: Processes inter-chain distances and angles with specialized constraints
- **Template Module**: Integrates multi-chain template information with chain-aware processing
- **Loss Functions**: Combine intra-chain and inter-chain quality metrics

For detailed information about the core AlphaFold 2 implementation, see [AlphaFold 2 Model Implementation](9-alphafold-2-model-implementation). For memory optimization techniques that apply to multimer scenarios, refer to [Memory Optimization Techniques](11-memory-optimization-techniques).

# Long Sequence Inference


Long sequence inference in OpenFold addresses the computational challenges of predicting protein structures for sequences exceeding typical memory constraints. This specialized mode enables researchers to work with large proteins and complexes that would otherwise exceed GPU memory limits by implementing strategic memory optimization techniques.

## Memory Optimization Architecture

OpenFold provides a comprehensive suite of memory management strategies specifically designed for long sequence inference. The architecture is built around three core optimization approaches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    A[Long Sequence Inference] --> B[Template Processing]
    A --> C[Attention Optimization]
    A --> D[Memory Management]
    
    B --> B1[Template Averaging]
    B --> B2[Template Offloading]
    
    C --> C1[Low-Memory Attention]
    C --> C2[DeepSpeed Evoformer Attention]
    C --> C3[FlashAttention]
    
    D --> D1[Dynamic Chunking]
    D --> D2[CPU Offloading]
    D --> D3[Inference-time Optimization]
```

## Configuration Options

### Long Sequence Mode Activation
The long sequence inference mode can be activated using the `--long_sequence_inference` flag in [`run_pretrained_openfold.py`](run_pretrained_openfold.py#L462). When enabled, this flag automatically configures optimal settings for memory conservation:

Sources: [`run_pretrained_openfold.py`](run_pretrained_openfold.py#L462-L465), [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L213-L223)

| Configuration Setting | Default Value | Long Sequence Value | Description |
|---------------------|---------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `globals.offload_inference` | False | True | Enables CPU offloading for inference |
| `globals.use_deepspeed_evo_attention` | False | True | Uses DeepSpeed memory-efficient attention |
| `globals.use_flash` | False | False | Disables FlashAttention for stability |
| `model.template.offload_inference` | False | True | Offloads template processing to CPU |
| `tune_chunk_size` (various stacks) | True | False | Disables automatic chunk size tuning |

### Template Processing Optimization
Template processing represents a major memory bottleneck for long sequences. OpenFold supports two mutually exclusive approaches:

Sources: [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L213-L223), [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L154-L158)

**Template Averaging (`average_templates`)**:
- Reduces memory footprint by averaging template features
- Similar to AlphaFold-Multimer approach
- Provides moderate memory savings with minimal performance impact

**Template Offloading (`offload_templates`)**:
- Moves template computations to CPU memory
- More aggressive memory optimization
- Trades speed for significantly reduced GPU memory usage

> [!TIP]
> Template processing is often the primary memory bottleneck for sequences over 2000 residues. Enabling either template averaging or offloading is crucial for successful inference on very long sequences.

## Attention Mechanism Optimization

### Low-Memory Attention (LMA)
Inference-time low-memory attention can be enabled in the model configuration, trading speed for vastly improved memory usage:

Sources: [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L30-L41), [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L159-L162)

```python
# Enable LMA with custom chunk sizes
config.globals.use_lma = True
config.globals.query_chunk_size = 1024
config.globals.key_chunk_size = 4096
```

**Default LMA Configuration**:
- Query chunk size: 1024
- Key chunk size: 4096
- These values represent a favorable tradeoff in most memory-constrained scenarios

### DeepSpeed Evoformer Attention
The DeepSpeed DS4Sci_EvoformerAttention kernel provides memory-efficient attention with significant performance benefits:

Sources: [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L30-L41), [`deepspeed_inference_test.py`](scripts/deepspeed_inference_test.py#L1-L55)

**Benefits**:
- 2-3x inference speedup without significant additional memory usage
- Automatic activation in long sequence mode (unless LMA is explicitly enabled)
- Requires DeepSpeed installation with DS4Science components

**Activation**:
```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    --use_deepspeed_evoformer_attention \
    # ... other arguments
```

### FlashAttention Considerations
FlashAttention provides optimization for shorter sequences but has limitations for long sequences:

Sources: [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L159-L162)

| Sequence Length | Recommended Setting | Notes |
|----------------|---------------------|-------|
| < 1000 residues | FlashAttention enabled | Best performance |
| > 1000 residues | FlashAttention disabled | Stability concerns |
| Long sequences | Disabled by default | Automatically set in long sequence mode |

## Chunking and Memory Management

### Dynamic Chunking Configuration
Chunking is enabled by default in inference mode, following AlphaFold 2 supplement section 1.11.8:

Sources: [`chunk_utils.py`](openfold/utils/chunk_utils.py#L1-L50), [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L166-L168)

**Chunking Controls**:
- `globals.chunk_size`: Controls chunk size for memory management
- `tune_chunk_size`: Enables automatic chunk size optimization
- Recommended to disable for very long sequences to avoid wasted computation time

**Configuration Examples**:
```python
# Disable chunking entirely
config.globals.chunk_size = None

# Manual chunk size setting
config.globals.chunk_size = 128
config.globals.tune_chunk_size = False
```

### CPU Offloading Strategies
OpenFold provides multiple levels of CPU offloading for extreme memory constraints:

Sources: [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L213-L223), [`tensor_utils.py`](openfold/utils/tensor_utils.py#L1-L50)

**Offloading Options**:

| Feature | Description | Memory Impact | Speed Impact |
|---------|-------------|---------------|--------------|
| `offload_inference` | General inference offloading | High | Moderate |
| `model.template.offload_inference` | Template-specific offloading | Medium | Low |
| `offload_templates` | Template stack offloading | High | Moderate |

## Performance Benchmarks and Practical Examples

### Memory Requirements
Using the most conservative settings, OpenFold can run inference on a 4600-residue complex with a single A100 GPU:

Sources: [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L167-L177)

**Hardware Requirements for Long Sequences**:

| Sequence Length | Minimum GPU Memory | Recommended GPU | Notes |
|----------------|-------------------|----------------|-------|
| < 2000 residues | 16GB | RTX 3090/A6000 | Standard optimization |
| 2000-3500 residues | 24GB | A100/H100 | Long sequence mode recommended |
| 3500-4600 residues | 40GB | A100 40GB+ | Conservative settings required |
| > 4600 residues | 80GB | Multiple GPUs | Experimental |

### Performance Comparison
Compared to AlphaFold's own memory offloading mode, OpenFold's implementation is considerably faster:

Sources: [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L175-L177)

**Benchmark Results**:
- 4600-residue complex: OpenFold completes in less than half the time of AlphaFold-Multimer
- Memory efficiency: 30-50% reduction in peak memory usage
- Speed improvement: 2-3x faster inference with DeepSpeed optimization

## Implementation Examples

### Basic Long Sequence Inference
```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    /path/to/fasta_dir \
    /path/to/template_mmcif_dir \
    --output_dir /path/to/output \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --long_sequence_inference \
    --model_device "cuda:0" \
    --uniref90_database_path /path/to/uniref90 \
    --mgnify_database_path /path/to/mgnify \
    --pdb70_database_path /path/to/pdb70 \
    --uniclust30_database_path /path/to/uniclust30 \
    --bfd_database_path /path/to/bfd
```

### Advanced Configuration with Custom Settings
```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    /path/to/fasta_dir \
    /path/to/template_mmcif_dir \
    --output_dir /path/to/output \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --long_sequence_inference \
    --model_device "cuda:0" \
    --experiment_config_json long_sequence_config.json \
    --use_deepspeed_evoformer_attention
```

**Example `long_sequence_config.json`**:
```json
{
    "globals": {
        "use_lma": true,
        "query_chunk_size": 512,
        "key_chunk_size": 2048,
        "chunk_size": 64,
        "tune_chunk_size": false
    },
    "model": {
        "template": {
            "average_templates": true,
            "offload_templates": false
        }
    }
}
```

> [!TIP]
> For sequences exceeding 3000 residues, consider combining multiple optimization strategies: enable DeepSpeed attention, use template averaging, and set conservative chunk sizes for maximum memory efficiency.

## Troubleshooting and Best Practices

### Common Issues and Solutions

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| CUDA out of memory | Insufficient GPU memory | Enable long sequence mode, reduce chunk sizes |
| Slow inference | Over-conservative settings | Enable DeepSpeed, increase chunk sizes |
| Instability | FlashAttention on long sequences | Disable FlashAttention, use LMA |
| Template errors | Memory bottleneck | Enable template averaging or offloading |

### Optimization Priority
For maximum effectiveness, apply optimizations in this order:
1. Enable long sequence inference mode
2. Use DeepSpeed Evoformer attention
3. Configure template processing (averaging preferred over offloading)
4. Adjust chunk sizes and disable automatic tuning
5. Enable LMA as a last resort

Sources: [`Inference.md`](docs/source/Inference.md#L154-L177), [`config.py`](openfold/config.py#L213-L223)

For further information on related topics, see [Memory Optimization Techniques](11-memory-optimization-techniques), [DeepSpeed Integration and Performance](16-deepspeed-integration-and-performance), and [Custom CUDA Kernels and FlashAttention](17-custom-cuda-kernels-and-flashattention).

# Single Sequence Mode and Embeddings



OpenFold's Single Sequence Mode represents a paradigm shift from traditional MSA-dependent protein structure prediction by leveraging precomputed protein language model embeddings. This approach eliminates the need for Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) generation, dramatically reducing computational overhead while maintaining competitive accuracy for many protein families.

## Architecture Overview

The Single Sequence Mode architecture utilizes a streamlined pipeline that replaces traditional MSA processing with ESM-1b embeddings. This fundamental change enables faster inference and reduces dependency on large sequence databases.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[FASTA Input] --> B[ESM-1b Embedding Generation]
    B --> C[PreembeddingEmbedder]
    C --> D[Simplified Evoformer Stack]
    D --> E[Structure Module]
    E --> F[3D Structure Prediction]
    
    G[Template Search] --> D
    H[Target Features] --> C
```

## Core Components

### PreembeddingEmbedder

The `PreembeddingEmbedder` ([embedders.py#L312-L405](openfold/model/embedders.py#L312-L405)) serves as the primary interface for sequence embeddings in single sequence mode. This specialized embedder processes ESM-1b embeddings alongside target features:

```python
class PreembeddingEmbedder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        tf_dim: int,              # Target features dimension
        preembedding_dim: int,   # ESM-1b embedding dimension (1280)
        c_z: int,                # Pair embedding dimension
        c_m: int,                # Single-sequence embedding dimension
        relpos_k: int,           # Relative position encoding window
    ):
```

The embedder performs three key transformations:
1. **Linear projection** of target features and pre-embeddings to match model dimensions
2. **Relative positional encoding** using residue index information
3. **Pair embedding construction** combining sequence information with spatial relationships

### Model Configuration

Single sequence mode is activated through specialized configuration presets. The `seq_mode_config` ([config.py#L924-L957](openfold/config.py#L924-L957)) defines the operational parameters:

```python
seq_mode_config = mlc.ConfigDict({
    "data": {
        "seqemb_mode": {
            "enabled": True,  # Enable sequence embedding mode
        },
    },
    "globals": {
        "seqemb_mode_enabled": True,
    },
    "model": {
        "preembedding_embedder": {
            "tf_dim": 22,
            "preembedding_dim": 1280,  # ESM-1b dimension
            "c_z": 128,
            "c_m": 256,
            "relpos_k": 32,
        },
        "extra_msa": {
            "enabled": False  # Disable Extra MSA Stack
        },
        "evoformer_stack": {
            "no_column_attention": True  # Disable column attention
        },
    }
})
```

> [!TIP]
> The configuration disables MSA-specific components (Extra MSA Stack, column attention) to optimize the architecture for single-sequence processing while maintaining the core Evoformer structure.

## Embedding Generation Pipeline

### Precompute Embeddings

OpenFold provides a dedicated script for bulk ESM-1b embedding generation:

```bash
python scripts/precompute_embeddings.py fasta_dir/ embeddings_output_dir/
```

The `EmbeddingGenerator` class ([precompute_embeddings.py#L62-L150](scripts/precompute_embeddings.py#L62-L150)) handles the embedding process:

1. **Sequence Loading**: Parses FASTA files and creates batched datasets
2. **ESM-1b Model Loading**: Downloads and initializes the ESM-1b model
3. **Batch Processing**: Generates embeddings with configurable token batch sizes
4. **Output Management**: Saves embeddings as `.pt` files in structured directories

### Runtime Embedding Generation

Alternatively, embeddings can be generated during inference without precomputation:

```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    fasta_dir \
    data/pdb_mmcif/mmcif_files/ \
    --config_preset "seq_model_esm1b_ptm" \
    --openfold_checkpoint_path openfold/resources/openfold_soloseq_params/seq_model_esm1b_ptm.pt
```

The main inference script ([run_pretrained_openfold.py#L175-L250](run_pretrained_openfold.py#L175-L250)) automatically detects sequence mode based on configuration presets:

```python
if args.config_preset.startswith("seq"):
    args.use_single_seq_mode = True
```

## Integration with Main Model

The `AlphaFold` model ([model.py#L1-L100](openfold/model/model.py#L1-L100)) dynamically selects the appropriate embedder based on mode:

```python
if self.seqemb_mode:
    # Use PreembeddingEmbedder for single sequence mode
    self.input_embedder = PreembeddingEmbedder(
        **self.config["preembedding_embedder"],
    )
else:
    # Use traditional InputEmbedder for MSA mode
    self.input_embedder = InputEmbedder(
        **self.config["input_embedder"],
    )
```

## Performance Characteristics

### Memory and Computational Efficiency

| Feature | Traditional MSA Mode | Single Sequence Mode |
|---------|---------------------|---------------------|
| **Database Requirements** | Large (UniRef90, MGnify, etc.) | None (except optional templates) |
| **Preprocessing Time** | Hours to days | Minutes to hours |
| **GPU Memory Usage** | High (MSA tensors) | Moderate (single embeddings) |
| **Inference Speed** | Slower (MSA processing) | Faster (direct embedding use) |

### Sequence Limitations

> [!TIP]
> The ESM-1b model imposes a maximum sequence length of 1022 residues. Sequences exceeding this limit are automatically truncated, making the approach unsuitable for very large proteins without segmentation strategies.

## Usage Patterns

### Template Integration

Single sequence mode supports template information integration through `.hhr` files placed in the embedding output directories. This enables hybrid approaches combining language model embeddings with structural templates:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[FASTA Files] --> B[Embedding Generation]
    C[HHR Files] --> D[Template Processing]
    B --> E[Combined Feature Input]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Structure Prediction]
```

### Configuration Presets

OpenFold provides specialized presets for single sequence mode:

- `seq_model_esm1b_ptm`: Uses ESM-1b embeddings with pTM head for confidence estimation
- `seq_model_esm1b`: Basic ESM-1b model without pTM confidence scores
